event.detail:
# Removed fixture option and welcome watcher match the retired terminal path

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR

Considered whether removing the fabricated-session exception and second-client watcher makes browser coverage fail or silently accepts the wrong terminal. Source refutes this concern for the assigned changes.

## Details

The same commit removes fabricatedTerminals, the automatic hostPremise fixture, its observeContext registration and the entire helpers/host-premise.ts module (git diff of those helpers inspected). helpers/evidence.ts:18-65 defines the replacement fixture without that option. restart-replace-progress.spec.ts:23-77 still creates an explicitly fabricated source for lifecycle progress and never needs the retired watch's absent-session exception. welcome.spec.ts:60-74 creates an authentication-only second client and checks shared welcome_seen behavior; it no longer imports or calls a deleted module. SPEC_impl.md, Terminal widget: the grid island, says: "Every terminal runs in a terminal host ... so the browser draws a grid stream with its own grid client" and Testing says: "Its stacks create new terminals, as shipped supervisors do." Removal of dual-renderer premise plumbing matches that contract. Reviewed only removal implications, not independent defects in retired implementation.

Suggested bucket: other if it were a defect; confidence: confirmed source refutation; proposed_drop: source refutation, synchronized helper API removal and grid-only contract above; possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no; this concern is confined to test setup and coverage, with no established security or user-work-loss route. No execution or reproduction performed.

event.detail:
# Grid-only assertions retain the identity, palette, focus and hit-target checks

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR

Considered whether deleting the old-renderer alternatives weakens or breaks the browser tests. The assigned assertions continue to inspect the terminal the product actually mounts.

## Details

SPEC_impl.md:1504-1513 states every terminal uses a grid client, with Dioxus owning surrounding UI rather than terminal content. terminal.js:4659-4667 publishes __farhelmGrid and __farhelmWs for the agent terminal, and :4848-4849 removes both at teardown. grid-terminal.js:341-368 constructs .grid-terminal, .grid-terminal-screen and the textarea.grid-terminal-input; :828-834 paints the grid element's default foreground/background. Those are exactly the handles/selectors the assigned patches retain. appearance.spec.ts:181-197 retains the actual component and samples its explicit colors; :294-300 still checks component identity, both colors and computed terminal backgrounds. replace.spec.ts:867-869 stamps the actual grid; :929-947 requires a defined different grid with an OPEN socket before inspecting the replacement's READY and full buffer, preserving the old-instance guard. The sidebar focus and hit-test selectors match the grid constructor. tooltip-coverage.spec.ts's exception still excludes its real hidden keyboard textarea. These are source refutations of the contemplated regressions, not runtime observations.

Suggested bucket: other if a test defect; confidence: confirmed source refutation; proposed_drop: actual constructor, paint and test-hook contracts match the remaining assertions; possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no; concern is test coverage, with no established security or user-work-loss route. This does not certify unrelated product behavior or all possible stale-singleton races. No execution or reproduction performed.

## Synthesis revision (turn 2)

The original considered consequence remains weakened/broken identity and UI assertions; this is still only a proposed refutation, with no parent drop accepted. Cross-checked f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e's helper migration and callers: helpers/term.ts:176-215 and :272-300 read the same __farhelmGrid model/socket for termText and waitForTermText. attachSession (:315-337) finishes with waitForSessionReady, whose terminal-readiness.ts:126-183 observation checks decoded session ID, tab selector, OPEN socket, replay and the actual hidden input. The old dual-renderer predicate had exactly the same limitation. Thus c2 must not be read as a claim that sentinel inequality alone proves arbitrary replacement identity. No deletion-induced loss of that independent URL check occurred, because the replaced code had none.

Checked the product-side caller supplying the identity this test relies on: lib.rs:2120-2125 keys SessionView by the selected session ID; session_view.rs:1701-1761 builds the primary path from that session's immutable ID, and :1831-1874 generation-fences deferred sync and unmounts on drop. terminal.js:2853-2868 tears down a changed path/generation before mounting, :3191-3226 cancels superseded pending mounts and checks attempt identity before mounting, and :4761-4805 cancels pending/deferred callbacks before closing the old socket. At :4659-4667 grid and socket are published synchronously for that primary mount. This source supports the ordinary replacement path's identity assumption, without certifying every hypothetical framework-ordering regression. A distinct product bug returning an unrelated terminal despite these contracts would need its own established source route; none was found in the assigned changes. Tests were not executed.

Checklist synthesis: source attachment readiness precedes input and marker stamping; absence during unmount cannot satisfy Boolean(term); the retained appearance object explicitly asserts unchanged identity after each palette action, so remount cannot silently count as live recoloring. The no-old-renderer changes preserve rather than manufacture readiness. No additional unsettled premise remains for the narrow deletion claim.
